summary: Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Guang Xing is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of London (SOAS) under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy Hugh Barrett. He held posts at the University of Hong Kong and the University of British Columbia.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1986–2004) and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2004.

Guankong (1903–1989) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a teacher at the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and became a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima (1919–2014) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied law at the University of Tokyo, trained under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa, founded Dogen Sangha International in 2007, and lectured at the University of Tokyo and Eastern Institute.

Gudrun Bühnemann works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Michael Hahn and Ernst Steinkellner, receiving a doctorate from the University of Vienna, and has been a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison since 1992.

Gudrun Melzer is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann. As of 2026, she is affiliated with the University of Munich, Göttingen Academy of Sciences, and International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held an academic post at the University of Ceylon, attested in 1991 and 2008.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Stig Wikander. She served at Uppsala University from around 1978 to 2003.
Gunnar Jarring (1907–2002) was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lund University (~1926–1933) and subsequently held an academic post there (~1933–1940).

Guo Jun is a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney. Trained under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin, he is attested as abbot of Mahabodhi Monastery in 2013.
Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University (~2000–2005) under Kenyu Mitomo, having also studied under Sheng Yen and several other teachers.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Columbia University. He taught religion at Columbia (1988–1999) and held the Kundan Kaur Kapany Chair in Sikh Studies at UCSB (1999–2015).

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga (1874–1957) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University. He held academic posts at Utrecht University (1924–1957) and the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944).

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart and later served there as a Senior Teaching Fellow in anthropology and sociology.

Gustaf John Ramstedt (1873–1950) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Helsinki (~1893–1902), he held posts at Helsinki (~1917–1941) and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1929).

Gustav Haloun (1898–1951) was a scholar of sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studies at Leipzig and Charles University, he directed at Göttingen (1931–1938) and held the Chair of Chinese Language and History at Cambridge (1938–1951).

Gustav Mensching (1901–1978) was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Rudolf Otto. He held academic posts at the University of Latvia (1927–1936) and the University of Bonn (1936).

Gustav Roth (1916–2008) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Munich and studied at Patna University. He worked at the University of Göttingen (1965–1981) and directed the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Gustav Salomon Oppert (1836–1908) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Bonn, Leipzig, and Halle-Wittenberg, as well as the Berlin University of the Arts, where he later held a post (~1894–1908).
